name: What should be in a luxury custom home contract?

mainEntity.name: What should a luxury custom home construction contract include?
mainEntity.text: What should a luxury custom home construction contract include?

acceptedAnswer.text: A luxury custom home contract should do more than set a price. It should clearly define the scope of work, included materials, finish levels, allowances, exclusions, payment milestones, schedule assumptions, and the process for approving changes. It should also explain who handles permits, inspections, site protection, subcontractor coordination, and warranty service after completion. For high-end projects, the level of detail matters because many disputes start when owners assume something is included that the contract does not explicitly cover. The contract should also make clear how long-lead items are handled and whether allowance overruns are billed separately. Homeowners should review the scope carefully with the builder and ask for clarification on anything vague before signing. A well-written contract protects both the project budget and the relationship between the owner and the builder.
acceptedAnswer.description: A strong luxury custom home contract should define scope, specifications, allowances, payment schedule, change order rules, timeline expectations, warranty terms, and responsibilities for permits and coordination. It should also identify what is excluded so there is no confusion later.
